biography.plain_text: Arturo López Willshaw was a Chilean art collector and millionaire who settled in France between the world wars. He inherited the fortune created by his father, Arturo López Pérez, in guano. Known as Arturito, he assembled an important collection of French decorative arts, including eighteenth-century furniture and exceptional gold and silver objects.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Versailles, Chilean collector Arturo López Willshaw paid for the restoration of the King's Chamber. His 1953 gift enabled Lyon weavers to recreate its gold and silver brocade from a surviving fragment held by the Mobilier National. He also supported restoration of the shell cottage in the grounds of Rambouillet.

López Willshaw brought that taste for royal interiors into his own house at Neuilly-sur-Seine. He remodelled the mansion with extensive work during the 1950s and commissioned a ballroom covered in shells, echoing the Rambouillet cottage. The house provided a setting for elaborate entertainments as well as his daily surroundings.
